title: Cancellation Fee and Restocking Schedule for Retrofit Project Classes
content:
# Cancellation Fee and Restocking Schedule

Stage fees and the supplier restocking fee for Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects, per project class. The stage fee is expressed as a portion of the contract value and depends on the stage the project had reached when it was cancelled; the restocking fee is the supplier's charge passed through on returned equipment.

| Project class | Cancelled after award, before equipment release (per cent) | Cancelled after equipment release (per cent) | Cancelled after mobilisation (per cent) | Supplier restocking fee (per cent) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Equipment Replacement Order | 5 | 20 | 45 | 25 |
| Planned Replacement Program | 5 | 20 | 45 | 25 |
| Controls Retrofit Project | 8 | 25 | 50 | 20 |
| Energy Retrofit Project | 8 | 25 | 55 | 20 |
| Turnkey Mechanical Upgrade Project | 10 | 30 | 60 | 18 |
| Design-Build Infrastructure Program | 12 | 35 | 65 | 15 |

## Reading the columns

- The three stage columns are alternatives: a cancelled project is charged at one of them, according to its stage.
- The stage fee rises with the stage in every class, and the awarded-stage fee of the two lowest classes is the same 5 per cent.
- The restocking fee falls as the class rises, from 25 per cent in the Equipment Replacement Order and the Planned Replacement Program to 15 per cent in the Design-Build Infrastructure Program.

## Hypothetical figures

An Energy Retrofit Project at USD 200000 carries a stage fee of 8 per cent (USD 16000) if cancelled after award and before equipment release, 25 per cent (USD 50000) if cancelled after equipment release, and 55 per cent (USD 110000) if cancelled after mobilisation. Its supplier restocking fee is 20 per cent.
